answer.answer: The study can't answer the question. The validity gate kept none of the runs, so there is no evidence on which combinations of sideways plan error and hand-off speed make the ego leave its lane, and none of the 5 hardest cases was found or confirmed. The goal status agrees: no challenging setting was confirmed. The first five runs were rejected with a HALT verdict. Every later run was rejected with no reason recorded. This is a failure of the study's runs, not a sign that VaVAM is safe at these settings. Also, the rejected runs list the controller as "linear", not VaVAM, so even those attempts may not have tested the policy the question is about.
open: Why the runs failed the gate. The first five runs, at the ±0.5 m, 1.4x corners, ended in HALT. All later runs were rejected with no verdict recorded, which points to a problem in the pipeline or the gate rather than in the runs' results. This needs to be diagnosed and fixed before any rerun.
Which controller ran. The rejected runs are labelled 'linear', not VaVAM. Check that the policy under test is the one configured before spending more budget.
A quick check before the full search. Rerun one or two runs at bias 0, speed 1.0 on scenes that passed at 0 delay (for example clipgt-023b7fcc or clipgt-096988dd), and check that the gate keeps them.

The question itself, which remains wholly open. Once runs are kept, search the large-bias, high-speed corners (±0.3 to ±0.5 m at 1.2x to 1.4x) across the 12 scenes. Then repeat promising settings about 3 to 5 times each, to confirm 5 settings on distinct scenes whose failure-rate range lies above 0.5. Use closest approach to rank near misses if nothing fails.
